```{r}
#| label: setup
#| cache: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ape)
library(knitr)
library(here)

source(here("R", "phylo_metrics.R"))

tab <- \(f) read_csv(here("output", "tables", paste0(f, ".csv")), show_col_types = FALSE)
f2 <- \(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)
ci <- \(m, lo, hi) paste0(f2(m), " [", f2(lo), ", ", f2(hi), "]")
pct <- \(x) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = 0), "%")
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))
```

# Summary {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: summary-numbers
w98 <- tab("step2_within_div_variance")
w99 <- tab("t99_within_cell_variance")
r2b <- tab("t99_cells_vs_phylo_r2")
get_w <- \(w, m, col) w[[col]][w$metric == m]
```

- **Phylogenetic metrics in these multitrophic experiments mostly encode trophic
  structure.** In both experiments every composition is assembled from
  macrophytes, grazers and predators, and the plant–animal divergence dominates
  phylogenetic distances. Once the design is accounted for (richness in T98;
  functional-group composition × richness in T99), little variance in the
  metrics of the stocked communities remains: in T98,
  `r pct(get_w(w98, "PD_init", "within_div_share"))` (PD) and
  `r pct(get_w(w98, "MPD_init", "within_div_share"))` (MPD), although VPD keeps
  `r pct(get_w(w98, "VPD_init", "within_div_share"))`; in T99,
  `r pct(get_w(w99, "PD_init", "within_cell_share"))`–`r pct(get_w(w99, "VPD_init", "within_cell_share"))`
  for PD, MPD and VPD.
- **No credible effect of phylogenetic diversity on productivity, respiration
  or decomposition** at fixed richness/design cell, for any metric, for initial
  or final composition, in either experiment.
- **Across trophic configurations (T99), a single metric is an imperfect
  summary of trophic structure:** design cells account for
  `r pct(r2b$r2_comp[r2b$resp == "prod" & r2b$model == "cells"])` (productivity) and
  `r pct(r2b$r2_comp[r2b$resp == "resp" & r2b$model == "cells"])` (respiration) of
  among-composition variance; VPD alone for
  `r pct(r2b$r2_comp[r2b$resp == "prod" & r2b$model == "rich_VPD"])` and
  `r pct(r2b$r2_comp[r2b$resp == "resp" & r2b$model == "rich_VPD"])`; PD for none.
- **The acid pulse strongly depressed respiration (≈ −1 SD) and, less,
  productivity, followed by recovery of respiration.** Phylogenetic metrics did
  not robustly modulate resistance or recovery of productivity and respiration
  (the apparent T99 effect depends on a single composition). In T99 only,
  higher PD/MPD was associated with a larger post-pulse increase in
  decomposition (robust to leaving out single compositions at the 95% level),
  but this was not replicated in T98 and is one of ~48 modulation tests; we
  treat it as exploratory.
- **Why this matters:** Srivastava et al. (2012) argued that phylogenetic
  diversity may predict ecosystem function "from single-trophic to complex
  networks". Experiments manipulating more than two trophic levels are rare;
  these two are among the few, and they show that whole-community phylogenetic
  metrics largely restate trophic structure.
- **Box (exploratory):** a Diversity–Interaction-type model with
  phylogenetically structured species identity effects is not identifiable with
  these designs (posterior ≈ prior for the phylogenetic share).

# Data and design

## Experiments

```{r}
#| label: tbl-design
#| tbl-cap: "Design of the two mesocosm experiments (derived from the original spreadsheets)."
t98 <- read_csv(here("data", "derived", "bef_long.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
t99 <- read_csv(here("data", "derived", "t99_long.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
tibble(
  ` ` = c("Tanks", "Compositions", "Tanks per composition", "Richness levels (stocked)",
          "Functional-group (FG) composition", "Acid pulse", "Sampling periods", "Responses"),
  `T98 (Downing & Leibold 2002)` = c(
    n_distinct(t98$tank), n_distinct(t98$comp), "4", "3, 9, 15 (1, 3, 5 per FG)",
    "always macrophytes + grazers + predators", "after period 2; 2 of 4 tanks per composition",
    "6", "productivity, respiration, decomposition"),
  `T99 (Downing 2005)` = c(
    n_distinct(t99$tank), paste(n_distinct(t99$comp) - 1, "+ 1 no-species control"), "4", "6, 18",
    "M, G, MG, GP, MGP", "between periods 4 and 5 (inferred); 2 of 4 tanks",
    "13 (irregular, days 0–72); decomposition in 9", "productivity, respiration, decomposition")
) |> kable()
```

## Data sources and corrections

All derived data are rebuilt from Amy Downing's original spreadsheets
(`data/raw/`), which are kept read-only.

- **T98 ecosystem functioning**: sheet "ecosystem functioning T98 long". The
  legacy file `data_diogo.csv` is a rounded copy with one error (`dist = 6`
  for tank 5, period 6; the original has 1).
- **T98 initial (stocked) composition**: Table 1 of the Supplementary
  Information of Downing & Leibold (2002), parsed by
  `analysis/00a_initial_composition.py` (non-italic values = stocked;
  "0" = stocked and extinct; italic = invader). All 21 compositions contain
  exactly 1, 3 or 5 species per FG, and survivors + invaders reproduce the
  final composition (`treat.txt`) exactly.
- **T99 composition**: sheet "FG expt design T99". Species codes were mapped to
  tip labels by matching presence patterns against `Ecology2005.txt`; the two
  mismatches are errors in `Ecology2005.txt` (composition 5 lacks
  *L. clamitans*; composition 16 lists *Buenoa* instead of *Dineutus*), as
  confirmed by final biomass.
- **Legacy analyses (2014–2019) must not be reused.** MPD and MNTD were
  attached with `rep(mpd, each = 12)` although each composition has 24 rows,
  which silently recycled the vector and assigned wrong values to 480 of 504
  rows; the PD column was computed on an earlier tree (+21.1 Myr in nine
  compositions) and PSV of composition 6 was copied from composition 5.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pd-checks
#| tbl-cap: "T98 final-composition metrics recomputed with the re-dated tree, compared with the legacy data file."
tab("pd_checks") |>
  distinct(comp, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  transmute(comp, SR, PD = round(PD, 1), PD_legacy = round(PD_legacy, 1), dPD = round(dPD, 1),
            PSV = round(PSV, 3), PSV_legacy = round(PSV_legacy, 3)) |>
  kable()
```

## Ecosystem functioning over time

```{r}
#| label: fig-timeseries
#| fig-cap: "Mean (± SE across tanks) productivity, respiration and decomposition over sampling periods, by acid-pulse treatment. Dashed line: timing of the pulse."
#| fig-height: 6
ts <- bind_rows(
  t98 |> transmute(exp = "T98", time, dist, productivity = prod, respiration = resp, decomposition = dc, pulse = 2.5),
  t99 |> filter(comp > 0) |> transmute(exp = "T99", time, dist, productivity = prod, respiration = resp, decomposition = dc, pulse = 4.5)
) |>
  pivot_longer(productivity:decomposition, names_to = "response") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  summarise(m = mean(value), se = sd(value) / sqrt(n()), .by = c(exp, response, time, dist, pulse))
ggplot(ts, aes(time, m, colour = factor(dist), group = dist)) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = pulse), linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = m - se, ymax = m + se), size = 0.2) + geom_line() +
  facet_grid(response ~ exp, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("0" = "#1565C0", "1" = "#E65100"), labels = c("control", "acid pulse")) +
  labs(x = "Sampling period", y = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

# Phylogenies and phylogenetic metrics

Pseudochronograms were assembled from node ages (TimeTree) and dated with
`bladj` (Phylocom). T98 uses the 21-species tree for the stocked composition
and the re-dated 19-species tree (two macrophytes extinct in all tanks) for
the final composition; T99 uses a 24-species tree. Metrics follow the three
dimensions of Tucker et al. (2016), fixed *a priori*: PD (richness), MPD
(divergence) and VPD (regularity); MNTD is shown for completeness.

```{r}
#| label: fig-trees
#| fig-cap: "Pseudochronograms (Myr) of the species pools. Colours: macrophytes (green), grazers (blue), predators (orange)."
#| fig-height: 6
fg_col <- c(macrophyte = "#2E7D32", grazer = "#1565C0", predator = "#E65100")
si <- read_csv(here("data", "derived", "si_table1_long.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |> distinct(species, group)
tr98 <- read.tree(here("data", "raw", "phylogeny", "phylog_dated_2002_21spp_4b4da4d.txt")) |> fix_tip_labels()
tr99 <- read.tree(here("data", "raw", "phylogeny", "phylog_dated_2005.txt")) |> fix_tip_labels()
plants <- "Potamogeton|Myriophyllum|Elodea|Ceratophyllum|Vallisneria|Utricularia|Sagittaria"
grazers <- "Lithobates|Crangonyx|Hyalella|Helisoma|Physa|corixa"
fg_of <- \(x) case_when(str_detect(x, plants) ~ "macrophyte", str_detect(x, grazers) ~ "grazer", TRUE ~ "predator")
stopifnot(all(fg_of(si$species) == si$group))
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 1, 2, 1))
for (tr in list(T98 = tr98, T99 = tr99)) {
  plot(tr, cex = 0.6, tip.color = fg_col[fg_of(tr$tip.label)], label.offset = 10)
  axisPhylo(cex.axis = 0.7)
}
```

## Metrics track the design

```{r}
#| label: fig-within-share
#| fig-cap: "Share of the variance of each metric among compositions that lies within design strata (T98: richness level; T99: FG composition × richness). Initial = stocked composition; final = realized composition at the end of the experiment."
shares <- bind_rows(
  w98 |> transmute(exp = "T98", metric, share = within_div_share),
  w99 |> filter(!str_detect(metric, "MNTD")) |> transmute(exp = "T99", metric, share = within_cell_share)
) |>
  separate(metric, c("metric", "composition"), sep = "_") |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, c("PD", "MPD", "VPD")))
ggplot(shares, aes(metric, share, fill = composition)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~exp) + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(init = "#7B1FA2", final = "#F9A825")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Variance within design strata", fill = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-branch-sens
```

# Statistical models

## Model structure

All models were fitted in `brms` (Bürkner 2017) with CmdStan. Responses were
standardized (z-scores) so that priors are on a common scale; productivity and
respiration contain negative values in T99 (oxygen-based estimates), so log
transformation was not used except for T98 respiration.

For tank $j$ in composition $c[j]$ at sampling period $t$, the primary model
(step 2) is:

### DAG

```{r}
#| label: fig-dag
#| fig-cap: "Directed acyclic graph of the primary model (T99 version; in T98 the design cells are richness levels with level-specific slopes). σ varies by period for productivity and respiration; decomposition has constant σ, Student-t errors and, in T99, no AR(1) term."
#| out-width: "100%"
DiagrammeR::grViz("
digraph bef_dag {

  graph [rankdir=TB, fontname=Helvetica, bgcolor=transparent,
         nodesep=0.5, ranksep=0.75, pad=0.4]
  node [fontname=Helvetica, fontsize=11]

  # Priors
  node [shape=hexagon, style=filled, fillcolor='#EDE7F6',
        color='#7B1FA2', fontcolor='#4A148C']
  Pb  [label='α, β, γ, δ, θ ~ N(0, 1²)']
  Ps  [label='σ_comp, σ_tank ~ Exp(2)']
  Pa  [label='φ ~ N(0, 0.5²), |φ| < 1']
  Pe  [label='prod, resp: log σ_t = κ₀ + κ_t,\nκ ~ N(0, 1²); dc: σ ~ Exp(1)']

  # Parameters
  node [shape=ellipse, style=filled, fillcolor='#FFF9C4',
        color='#F9A825', fontcolor='#212121']
  b   [label='α_cell, β (phylo slope),\nγ_t, δ, θ (pulse)']
  s_c [label='σ_comp\ncomposition SD']
  s_k [label='σ_tank\ntank SD']
  phi [label='φ\nAR(1)']
  sig [label='σ_t\nresidual SD']

  # Observed data
  node [shape=rect, style=filled, fillcolor='#E3F2FD',
        color='#1565C0', fontcolor='#0D47A1']
  X   [label='X: design cell, period,\npulse × post-pulse']
  Z   [label='z_w(PD | MPD | VPD)_c\nwithin-cell standardized']

  # Latent
  node [shape=ellipse, style=filled, fillcolor='#E8F5E9',
        color='#2E7D32', fontcolor='#1B5E20']
  u_c [label='u_c (composition RE)\nc = 1…21 (T98), 26 (T99)']
  u_k [label='v_j (tank RE)\nj = 1…84 (T98), 104 (T99)']
  e   [label='ε_tj = φ ε_(t−1)j + e_tj']
  eta [label='μ_tj\nlinear predictor']

  # Response
  node [shape=doubleoctagon, style=filled, fillcolor='#FFECB3',
        color='#E65100', fontcolor='#BF360C']
  Y [label='y_tj (standardized\nprod, resp, dc)']

  Pb -> b   [style=dashed, color='#9C27B0']
  Ps -> s_c [style=dashed, color='#9C27B0']
  Ps -> s_k [style=dashed, color='#9C27B0']
  Pa -> phi [style=dashed, color='#9C27B0']
  Pe -> sig [style=dashed, color='#9C27B0']

  s_c -> u_c [color='#2E7D32']
  s_k -> u_k [color='#2E7D32']
  phi -> e   [color='#2E7D32']

  b   -> eta
  X   -> eta [label=' Xα', color='#1565C0']
  Z   -> eta [label=' βz', color='#1565C0']
  u_c -> eta [color='#2E7D32']
  u_k -> eta [color='#2E7D32']
  e   -> eta [color='#2E7D32']

  eta -> Y
  sig -> Y [color='#E65100']

  {rank=source; Pb; Ps; Pa; Pe}
  {rank=same;   b; s_c; s_k; phi; sig}
  {rank=same;   X; Z}
  {rank=same;   u_c; u_k; e}
  {rank=sink;   Y}
}
")
```

### Formal equations (Zuur & Ieno 2016)

**Stage 1 — Observation model**

$$
y_{tj} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_{tj},\, \sigma_t^2) \quad \text{(prod, resp)}, \qquad
y_{tj} \sim t_\nu(\mu_{tj},\, \sigma) \quad \text{(dc)}
$$

**Stage 2 — Linear predictor**

$$
\mu_{tj} = \alpha_{\text{cell}[c]} + \beta\, z^{w}_{c} + \gamma_t +
\delta\,\text{Pulse}_j + \theta\,(\text{Pulse}_j \times \text{Post}_t) +
u_{c[j]} + v_j + \varepsilon_{tj}
$$

In T98, $\beta$ is estimated separately for each richness level
($\beta_{\text{div}[c]}$) and the average slope is derived. In step 3 the
pulse effect is split into resistance (first sampling(s) after the pulse) and
recovery phase (later samplings), each by richness level, and modulated by
$z^w_c$: $+\,\eta_E\,(\text{Pulse}\times\text{Early}\times z^w) + \eta_L\,(\text{Pulse}\times\text{Late}\times z^w)$.

**Stage 3 — Random effects and residual autocorrelation**

$$
u_c \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\text{comp}}), \qquad
v_j \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\text{tank}}), \qquad
\varepsilon_{tj} = \phi\, \varepsilon_{(t-1)j} + e_{tj}
$$

$$
\log \sigma_t = \kappa_0 + \kappa_t \quad \text{(prod, resp; in T99 with sum-to-zero contrasts)}
$$

The AR(1) term is omitted for T99 decomposition (see @sec-ppc).

**Stage 4 — Priors** (see @sec-priors)

**Within-stratum standardization of the phylogenetic predictor**

$$
z^w_c = \frac{x_c - \bar{x}_{s[c]}}{\sqrt{\sum_c (x_c - \bar{x}_{s[c]})^2 / (n - n_s)}}
$$

where $s[c]$ is the design stratum of composition $c$.

## Priors {#sec-priors}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-priors
#| tbl-cap: "Priors (standardized responses)."
tribble(
  ~Parameter, ~Prior, ~Justification,
  "Fixed effects (cells, periods, pulse, phylogenetic slopes)", "N(0, 1)", "Weakly informative on the z-scale: effects of ±2 SD are plausible, larger ones rare",
  "σ_comp, σ_tank", "Exponential(2)", "Prior mean 0.5 SD; among-unit SDs larger than the total SD are implausible",
  "σ (constant)", "Exponential(1)", "Residual SD below the total SD of 1",
  "log σ_t: intercept and period effects (prod, resp)", "N(0, 1)", "Allows several-fold changes in residual SD among periods (observed: up to 1.5-fold in T98, 3–5-fold in T99)",
  "AR(1) coefficient φ", "N(0, 0.5), bounded (−1, 1)", "Moderate autocorrelation most plausible",
  "Student-t ν (dc)", "Gamma(2, 0.1)", "brms default; allows heavy to near-Gaussian tails"
) |> kable()
```

### Prior predictive check

```{r}
#| label: tbl-prior-pred
#| tbl-cap: "Prior predictive distribution of the standardized responses (primary MPD models; 200 prior draws). Observed SD = 1."
tab("prior_predictive_summary") |>
  transmute(Experiment = exp, Response = response,
            `Median SD of prior draws` = round(prior_pred_sd_median, 2),
            `99th percentile of |y_rep|` = round(prior_pred_q99_abs, 1),
            `Share within observed range` = pct(share_within_obs_range)) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-prior-pred
#| fig-cap: "Prior predictive density (light) vs observed standardized response (dark)."
#| fig-subcap: ["T98 decomposition", "T98 productivity", "T98 respiration", "T99 decomposition", "T99 productivity", "T99 respiration"]
#| layout-ncol: 3
include_graphics(here("figures", "prior_predictive", paste0(rep(c("T98", "T99"), each = 3), "_", c("dc", "prod", "resp"), ".png")))
```

The priors are weakly informative for decomposition. For productivity and
respiration, the prior on the residual-SD submodel is diffuse on the outcome
scale (the sum of an intercept and period effects on the log scale), producing
a long prior-predictive tail; power-scaling shows that posteriors are not sensitive
to it (@sec-priorsense).

# Computation and model checking

## MCMC diagnostics

Four chains, 2000 iterations each (1000 warm-up), `adapt_delta = 0.95`. Models
that did not meet R-hat ≤ 1.01 and bulk/tail ESS ≥ 400 were automatically
refitted with 4000 iterations and `adapt_delta = 0.99`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-diagnostics
#| tbl-cap: "Convergence summary by analysis (worst value across all parameters and models)."
diag_all <- bind_rows(
  tab("step2_diagnostics") |> mutate(analysis = "T98 step 2"),
  tab("step3_diagnostics") |> mutate(analysis = "T98 step 3"),
  tab("t99_diagnostics") |> mutate(analysis = "T99 steps 2–3"),
  tab("t99_species_identity_diagnostics") |> mutate(analysis = "T99 Box (species identity)")
)
diag_all |>
  summarise(models = n(), max_rhat = round(max(max_rhat), 3),
            min_ess_bulk = round(min(min_ess_bulk)), min_ess_tail = round(min(min_ess_tail)),
            divergences = sum(divergences), treedepth_hits = sum(max_treedepth_hits), .by = analysis) |>
  kable()
```

Maximum-treedepth warnings occurred only in T99 decomposition models refitted
with 8000 post-warm-up transitions (≤ 0.5% of transitions); they indicate
reduced sampling efficiency, not biased estimates, and all R-hat and ESS
criteria were met.

## Residual autocorrelation and variance structure

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ar1
#| tbl-cap: "T98: AR(1) coefficient and LOO comparison of models with and without AR(1) (elpd difference of the worse model)."
tab("ar1_check") |>
  transmute(response, `AR(1)` = ci(ar1_mean, ar1_q2.5, ar1_q97.5),
            `Δelpd (± SE)` = paste0(f2(elpd_diff), " ± ", f2(se_diff))) |>
  kable()
```

The residual SD of productivity and respiration varies among periods
(up to 1.5-fold in T98, 3–5-fold in T99, largest right after the pulse), as
shown by grouped posterior predictive checks of earlier constant-σ fits. In
T99, a first fit with Student-t errors absorbed this as very heavy tails
(ν ≈ 2). The final models use a distributional submodel for σ; the Student-t
results are kept as a sensitivity analysis (`output/tables/sensitivity/`).

For T99 decomposition, models with AR(1) failed to reproduce the mean of each
sampling period (grouped posterior predictive p = 0 or 1 in 7 of 10 periods,
with Gaussian or Student-t errors), whereas models without AR(1) did
(p = 0.42–0.64). Residual autocorrelation of decomposition is negligible
(T98: φ ≈ 0.05), so AR(1) was omitted for T99 decomposition.

## Posterior predictive checks {#sec-ppc}

Density overlays are a weak check; each panel below also compares the observed
mean and SD within each sampling period and design stratum with their
posterior predictive distributions, and shows LOO-PIT calibration.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ppc-grouped
#| tbl-cap: "Grouped posterior predictive checks of the primary MPD models: number of groups (periods or strata) whose observed statistic falls outside the central 90% of its posterior predictive distribution (p < 0.05 or p > 0.95)."
tab("ppc_grouped_pvalues") |>
  summarise(groups = n(), outside_90 = sum(p < 0.05 | p > 0.95), .by = c(exp, response, stat, group)) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc
#| fig-cap: "Posterior predictive checks of the primary MPD models (initial composition)."
#| fig-subcap: ["T98 productivity", "T98 respiration", "T98 decomposition", "T99 productivity", "T99 respiration", "T99 decomposition"]
#| layout-ncol: 2
include_graphics(here("figures", "ppc_detail", paste0(rep(c("T98", "T99"), each = 3), "_", c("prod", "resp", "dc"), ".png")))
```

LOO-PIT is shown only for models without AR(1), because with AR terms the
pointwise log-likelihood is conditional on the previous observation and
PSIS-LOO is not valid. Period means are reproduced in all models. The SD
within some sampling periods is not reproduced for T99 respiration (and, to
a lesser degree, productivity and decomposition), even when σ varies by
period. None of four alternative variance structures removed this misfit,
and the focal slope was insensitive to them:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-var-sens
#| tbl-cap: "T99: grouped posterior predictive checks and the within-cell MPD slope under alternative variance structures (number of periods whose observed SD or mean falls outside the central 90% of the posterior predictive distribution)."
tab("t99_variance_sensitivity") |>
  transmute(response, variant, `SD outside` = paste0(sd_outside, "/", periods),
            `mean outside` = paste0(mean_outside, "/", periods),
            `MPD slope` = ci(slope, q2.5, q97.5), max_rhat = round(max_rhat, 3)) |>
  kable()
```

## Prior sensitivity (priorsense) {#sec-priorsense}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-priorsense
#| tbl-cap: "Power-scaling sensitivity of the focal parameters [CITAR: priorsense — Kallioinen et al.; verify]. Values > 0.05 indicate sensitivity."
tab("prior_sensitivity") |>
  filter(str_detect(variable, "MPD|dist")) |>
  mutate(across(c(prior, likelihood), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  kable()
```

All focal parameters are likelihood-dominated. The single flag ("potential
prior–likelihood conflict") concerns the T98 productivity pulse effect,
whose prior sensitivity (0.053) is at the threshold; its posterior
(≈ −0.45 SD) lies well within the N(0, 1) prior.

# Results — T98

## Metrics fixed *a priori*, within richness levels

```{r}
#| label: fig-t98-step2
#| fig-cap: "T98: average within-richness slopes of PD, MPD and VPD (initial and final composition); 95% (thick) and 98.33% (thin) credible intervals."
#| fig-height: 4
forest <- \(df, x = "predictor") ggplot(df, aes(mean, .data[[x]])) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = q0.83, xmax = q99.17), linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = q2.5, xmax = q97.5), linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2) + labs(x = "Effect (SD of response per SD of predictor)", y = NULL)
s98 <- tab("step2_slopes") |> filter(div == "average") |>
  mutate(predictor = str_remove(predictor, "^zw_"))
forest(s98) + facet_wrap(~response)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-t98-varcomp
#| tbl-cap: "T98: among-composition SD (posterior median) in the richness-only model and with each metric. Among-composition variance is small, so the share explained by a metric cannot be estimated reliably (draw-wise ratios span from strongly negative to ~1)."
tab("step2_r2_composition") |>
  transmute(response, predictor = str_remove(predictor, "^zw_"),
            `σ_comp (richness only)` = f2(sd_comp_base), `σ_comp (with metric)` = f2(sd_comp_x)) |>
  kable()
```

## Step 3: disturbance

```{r}
#| label: fig-t98-step3
#| fig-cap: "T98: acid-pulse effects by richness level (resistance = period 3; recovery = periods 4–6 minus period 3), from the initial-MPD model."
#| fig-height: 3.5
d3 <- tab("step3_disturbance_effects")
d3 |> filter(predictor == "zw_MPD_init", !str_detect(term, "modulates|recovery phase")) |>
  mutate(div = factor(div, c("S3", "S9", "S15"))) |>
  forest("div") + facet_grid(term ~ response) + labs(y = "Richness")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-t98-mod
#| tbl-cap: "T98: modulation of resistance and recovery phase by phylogenetic metrics (within-richness standardized)."
d3 |> filter(str_detect(term, "modulates")) |>
  transmute(response, predictor = str_remove(predictor, "^zw_"), term,
            `95% CI` = ci(mean, q2.5, q97.5), `98.33% CI` = ci(mean, q0.83, q99.17)) |>
  kable()
```

# Results — T99

## Within design cells

```{r}
#| label: fig-t99-a
#| fig-cap: "T99: slopes of within-cell standardized metrics."
#| fig-height: 3.5
tab("t99_step2_slopes") |> mutate(predictor = str_remove(predictor, "^zw_")) |>
  forest() + facet_wrap(~response)
```

## Can a phylogenetic metric replace the trophic design?

```{r}
#| label: fig-t99-b
#| fig-cap: "T99: proportion of among-composition variance (relative to a richness-only model) explained by a single globally standardized metric or by the design cells (FG composition × richness). Bars: 95% CI of the draw-wise ratio (truncated at 0)."
#| fig-height: 3.5
tab("t99_cells_vs_phylo_r2") |>
  filter(model != "rich_only") |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, c("rich_PD", "rich_MPD", "rich_VPD", "cells"),
                        c("PD", "MPD", "VPD", "design cells"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(r2_comp, model)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = pmax(q2.5, 0), xmax = q97.5), colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) + facet_wrap(~resp) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Among-composition variance explained", y = NULL)
```

## Disturbance and its modulation

```{r}
#| label: fig-t99-c
#| fig-cap: "T99: acid-pulse effects by richness (resistance = periods 5–6; recovery = periods 7–13 minus 5–6)."
#| fig-height: 3.5
c99 <- tab("t99_step3_disturbance")
c99 |> filter(predictor == "zw_MPD_init", !str_detect(term, "modulates|recovery phase")) |>
  mutate(rich = factor(rich, c("S6", "S18"))) |>
  forest("rich") + facet_grid(term ~ response) + labs(y = "Richness")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-t99-mod
#| tbl-cap: "T99: modulation of resistance and recovery phase by phylogenetic metrics."
c99 |> filter(str_detect(term, "modulates")) |>
  transmute(response, predictor = str_remove(predictor, "^zw_"), term,
            `95% CI` = ci(mean, q2.5, q97.5), `98.33% CI` = ci(mean, q0.83, q99.17)) |>
  kable()
```

### Influence of single compositions

```{r}
#| label: fig-influence
#| fig-cap: "T99: effects whose 95% interval excluded zero, re-estimated leaving out each composition in turn (red: full data). Top row: modulation of the recovery phase; last panel: within-cell MPD slope on decomposition."
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 10
inf <- tab("t99_influence_mpd_recovery")
inf |> mutate(dropped = fct_reorder(dropped, mean),
              panel = paste(response, str_remove(predictor, "^zw_"), sep = ": ")) |>
  ggplot(aes(mean, dropped, colour = dropped == "none")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = q2.5, xmax = q97.5)) + geom_point() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "black", `TRUE` = "red"), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ effect + panel, nrow = 2, scales = "free_x") +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6)) +
  labs(x = "Effect", y = "Composition left out")
```

The negative MPD × recovery-phase effect disappears when composition 12 (cell
GP_6) is removed. In that composition the two tanks assigned to the pulse
already had lower productivity and respiration than the two control tanks
before the pulse and higher values afterwards, so much of its apparent
"recovery" reflects a pre-treatment imbalance. We therefore do not interpret
this effect.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-influence
#| tbl-cap: "Leave-one-composition-out summary: number of the 26 refits whose 95% and 98.33% intervals exclude zero."
inf |> filter(dropped != "none") |>
  summarise(full = round(mean[1], 2), min = round(min(mean), 2), max = round(max(mean), 2),
            `95% excl. 0` = sum(q2.5 > 0 | q97.5 < 0), `98.33% excl. 0` = sum(q0.83 > 0 | q99.17 < 0),
            .by = c(response, predictor, effect)) |>
  mutate(full = round(inf$mean[inf$dropped == "none"][match(paste(response, predictor, effect),
           paste(inf$response, inf$predictor, inf$effect)[inf$dropped == "none"])], 2)) |>
  kable()
```

For decomposition, the within-cell MPD slope depends on composition 11
(without it 0.04), whereas the positive modulation of the post-pulse phase by
PD and MPD persists in most leave-one-out refits. Because T98 shows no such
effect, we report it as exploratory.

# Box — phylogenetically structured species identity effects (exploratory)

If species $i$ has an additive effect $b_i$ and composition $c$ contains
species in equal proportions $p_{ci} = 1/S_c$ (stocked composition), the
composition effect is $\mathbf{u} = \mathbf{P}\mathbf{b}$. With
$\mathbf{b} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \sigma^2_{\text{phy}}\mathbf{C} + \sigma^2_{\text{id}}\mathbf{I})$,
where $\mathbf{C}$ is the phylogenetic correlation matrix, composition effects
have covariance $\sigma^2_{\text{phy}}\mathbf{P}\mathbf{C}\mathbf{P}^\top + \sigma^2_{\text{id}}\mathbf{P}\mathbf{P}^\top$,
fitted as two composition-level random effects with known kernels (as in an
animal model), plus an iid composition term for non-additive effects. This is
the identity component of Diversity–Interaction models (Kirwan et al. 2009),
with a phylogenetic prior on species effects; with equal proportions, a
phylogenetically structured pairwise interaction term (Connolly et al. 2011)
reduces to $\theta\,\frac{S-1}{2S}\,\text{MPD}$, i.e. the MPD models above.

Kernels were projected orthogonally to the richness means and scaled to unit
mean diagonal. The phylogenetic and identity kernels are strongly aligned
(0.87 in T98, 0.67 in T99), so the model was fitted to T99 only and its
identifiability checked against prior-only fits.

```{r}
#| label: fig-box
#| fig-cap: "T99 Box: phylogenetic signal in species effects, σ²_phy / (σ²_phy + σ²_id), and share of non-additive composition variance; prior vs posterior (median and 95% interval)."
#| fig-height: 3
tab("t99_species_identity_variance") |>
  filter(quantity %in% c("phylo_signal", "share_nonadditive")) |>
  ggplot(aes(median, fit, colour = fit)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = q2.5, xmax = q97.5), linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_grid(quantity ~ response) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(prior = "#7B1FA2", posterior = "#F9A825"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-box-contraction
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior contraction (1 − posterior width / prior width of the 95% interval)."
tab("t99_species_identity_contraction") |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) |> kable()
```

The posterior of the phylogenetic share is practically identical to the prior
for productivity and respiration; for decomposition it shifts towards
phylogenetically structured effects but remains uninformative. Separating
phylogenetic from non-phylogenetic species effects would require designs in
which composition varies within trophic groups independently of trophic
structure.
